title: Sell Mineral Rights in Mentone, TX
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Mentone, TX
metaDescription: Mentone is the Loving County seat, population in the double digits, surrounded by some of the densest horizontal drilling in the Delaware Basin. We buy direct.
heroLead: Mentone might be the smallest county seat in America, but don't mistake that for a lack of activity underground.
intro: As the seat of Loving County, Mentone has a courthouse and not much else on the surface, yet the sections around it carry some of the highest well density anywhere in the Permian. That mismatch between the town's size and the drilling activity is the whole story here.

sections.heading: The courthouse matters more than the town
paragraphs: Even though almost nobody lives in Mentone itself, this is where the Loving County Clerk keeps the recorded deeds, assignments, and probate filings we need to confirm your mineral title. We work directly with those records regardless of where you personally live.

sections.heading: Dense multi-well development nearby
paragraphs: Sections around Mentone commonly carry multiple horizontal wellbores under a single surface location, targeting different Wolfcamp and Bone Spring benches. We check every unit tied to your acreage, since a tract here can easily be part of more spacing units than an owner realizes.

sections.heading: Ranching heritage under the rig count
paragraphs: Before the horizontal boom, this ground was almost entirely ranch land, and a lot of Mentone-area mineral owners are descendants of the families who originally held both the surface and the minerals together. We're used to tracing that ranching-family chain of title through decades of assignments to confirm exactly what's yours today.

faqs.question: Does it matter that almost nobody lives in Mentone?
faqs.answer: Not for your mineral interest. The Loving County Clerk's office here holds the recorded title documents we need regardless of population, and drilling activity around Mentone is dense despite the small town.

faqs.question: How many wells might be tied to my tract near Mentone?
faqs.answer: Potentially several, since sections here often carry multiple horizontal wellbores targeting different benches. We check every unit before quoting instead of only the well on your most recent check.

faqs.question: I live out of state and have never been to Mentone. Can I still sell?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's the norm for Loving County owners. We handle everything by mail and wire, no travel required.

faqs.question: My family originally held the ranch this acreage sits on. Does that affect the mineral sale?
faqs.answer: It usually just means a longer chain of title to confirm through the county clerk's records. Once we've verified current ownership, the mineral sale proceeds the same as any other interest.

faqs.question: Is there a minimum interest size you'll buy near Mentone?
faqs.answer: No set minimum. Given how many wells touch a typical Loving County tract, even a small fractional interest can carry real value, and we'll evaluate yours on its own record.
